title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is
abstract: arXiv:2611.25135v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). An LLM converted into a decision model answers a typed question about a response ("is the final answer correct?", "which step is the first error?") with a probability distribution, read in one forward pass, debiased over option orders and calibrated with about a hundred labels. Training Qwen3-1.7B with GRPO on MATH, this reference-free reward raises MATH500 accuracy from 72.2% to 76.8% (+4.65 points, p < 1e-4), matching training on the answer key (76.9%), while a random reward gains only +0.65. The gain grows with difficulty, from 44.8% to 51.7% on the hardest level. On the policy's own changing samples the reward stays calibrate

translated_title: 校准决策奖励：用知道自己有多确定的裁判来训练语言模型
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）只能教给语言模型其奖励所能识别的内容。答案检查器精确，但需要参考答案；学习得到的奖励模型和LLM裁判虽可通用于各种场景，但它们的分数并非概率。我们研究了RLCDR（基于校准决策奖励的强化学习）。将一个LLM转化为决策模型，以概率分布的形式回答关于回复的类型化问题（如“最终答案是否正确？"、“哪一步是第一个错误？"），仅需一次前向传播即可读取，对选项顺序进行了去偏处理，并用大约一百个标签完成校准。在MATH上使用GRPO训练Qwen3-1.7B，这种无需参考答案的奖励将MATH500准确率从72.2%提升至76.8%（+4.65个百分点，p < 1e-4），与使用标准答案训练的效果相当（76.9%），而随机奖励仅带来+0.65的提升。该增益随题目难度增加而增大，在最难的级别上从44.8%提升至51.7%。在策略自身不断变化的样本上，该奖励依然保持校准……
tldr: 该论文提出RLCDR方法，将LLM转化为输出概率分布且经过校准的决策模型作为无需参考答案的奖励信号用于强化学习训练，使Qwen3-1.7B在MATH500上的准确率提升4.65个百分点，达到与使用标准答案训练相当的水平，且提升幅度随题目难度增加而增大。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes RLCDR, which converts an LLM into a calibrated decision model that outputs probability distributions as a reference-free reward for RL training, improving Qwen3-1.7B's MATH500 accuracy by 4.65 points to match training with ground-truth answers, with gains growing as problem difficulty increases.
